summary: TerraAnáloga es una plataforma geoespacial Full-Stack diseñada para identificar análogos terrestres de futuras bases lunares (Artemis) y zonas de exploración marciana. Para resolver el desafío, desarrollamos una arquitectura que combina FastAPI y React/MapLibre para consumir datos satelitales en vivo de la NASA (GIBS, Earthdata) y la ESA (Copernicus). Evaluamos variables como temperatura de superficie (LST), polvo (AOD), relieve e iluminación mediante nuestro Índice de Fidelidad Analógica (IFA 5D), generando un ranking de 19 zonas críticas. Además, integramos un pipeline de teledetección para calcular NDVI/NDWI en tiempo real y visualizaciones con interpolación IDW. Es crucial porque acelera la investigación aeroespacial, permitiendo probar equipos y entrenar astronautas en entornos terrestres que simulan con precisión las extremas condiciones del espacio, reduciendo riesgos y costos de misión.
details:
Project Details:

What it does & How it works:
TerraAnáloga is a geospatial web platform that identifies Earth-based terrestrial analogs for future lunar (Artemis) and Martian exploration. It calculates a 5D Analogue Fidelity Index (IFA) based on five scientific dimensions: extreme cold (LST), dust/aerosols (AOD), ice/cryosphere (NDSI), shaded relief (DEM), and illumination. Users can interact with dynamic sliders to adjust the weight of each dimension in real-time, dynamically recalculating a ranked list of the best 19 analog sites worldwide.

Tools, Languages & Software used:

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, MapLibre GL JS (for 3D/2D interactive globes and IDW heatmap interpolation).
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, MongoDB Atlas (using geospatial 2dsphere indexing).
  • Data Pipelines & APIs: NASA Earthdata (CMR, HLS L30/S30), ESA Copernicus (Sentinel-2), NASA GIBS (MODIS/ASTER), Google Earth Engine (GEE), and GDAL for cloud-optimized GeoTIFF (COG) processing.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
Sending rovers and astronauts to the Moon or Mars is incredibly expensive and risky. TerraAnáloga accelerates mission planning and hardware testing by providing scientists with precise, data-driven Earth locations that perfectly mimic extreme extraterrestrial environments. This reduces mission costs, mitigates risks, and aids in astronaut geological training (analog missions).

How is it creative?:
Our creativity lies in bridging hardcore planetary science with an intuitive "Mission Control" UI. Instead of static maps, we implemented live satellite data ingestion (fetching real NDVI and thermal data from NASA/ESA), inverse distance weighting (IDW) for smooth, continuous global heatmaps, and a dynamic multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) that lets users "play" with planetary conditions.

Factors considered:
We focused heavily on data authenticity and security. We handled real satellite cloud masking (SCL/Fmask), handled API rate limits, and ensured secure token management for NASA Earthdata. We also optimized the frontend rendering using GPU-accelerated WebGL polygons and debounced state management to guarantee a smooth, lag-free user experience during live spatial queries.
